item.title: Approximation Error Approach
item.description: Every reconstruction model is an approximation: a coarser mesh than reality, pixels instead of a continuous conductivity, idealised electrodes.

item.title: Data and Noise
item.description: Where test data come from and what corrupts real data: synthetic conductivities, noise and modelling errors, and how to avoid overly optimistic results.

item.title: Plasma Nitrogen Fixation as a Moonshot
DiffPIR
item.description: DiffPIR (Zhu et al. 2023) integrates a diffusion model into a plug-and-play half-quadratic splitting scheme.

item.title: Outlook
item.description: Existing software, design principles for modular EIT solvers, open questions, and where the same mathematics could go next.

item.title: U-Net
item.description: The U-Net is a convolutional encoder–decoder with skip connections, the standard backbone for image-to-image tasks and for diffusion-model denoisers \varepsilon_\theta(x,t).

item.title: Diffusion Models for EIT
item.description: Recent work that combines diffusion or score-based priors with EIT: Diff-INR (Tong, Wang, Liu 2024): represents the conductivity as an implicit neural representation and uses a pretrained diffusion model as a generative regulariser during the reconstruction.

item.title: Diffusion Models on Finite Element Spaces
item.description: A diffusion model adds Gaussian noise to its samples (see DDPM Forward Process). On a uniform pixel grid “independent noise per pixel” is unambiguous.

item.title: Diffusion Models
item.description: Diffusion models learn a prior distribution by learning to reverse a gradual noising process.
